## 1a: mean function without NA handling

```{r}
v = c(1:50, NA, 55)
vector_mean <- function( df){
  tot = 0
  for ( element in df){
    tot = tot + element
  }
  return( tot / length(df))
}

vector_mean( v)

```

# 1b: mean with NA handled
```{r}
super_vector_mean <- function( vector , na.rm = F ){
  tot = 0
  for (element in vector){
    if( is.na(element)){
      if(na.rm){
        next
      }else{
        return( NA)
      }
    }
    tot = tot +element
  }
   n = sum( !is.na(vector))
  return( tot / n) 
}

super_vector_mean(v , na.rm = T)

mean( v , na.rm =F)

```
##### My loop base function for "mean" are expected to agree because I included lines that handle presence of NA values within passed vectore during iteration. The final sample size is also calculated taking NAs into consideration, hence the only actual values make up the final sample size.
